newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: TELECOM ADVISOR SET TO BE CHOSEN.
newsitem.headline: TELECOM ADVISOR SET TO BE CHOSEN.

text.p: The European Affairs Ministry said on Wednesday that it will today or tomorrow choose an advisor on the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom and may pick a runner up in case the first place bidder's price is too high.
An 11-member commission has been looking at offers from seven potential advisors in what is one of Lithuania's most important privatisations.
The commission is expected to decide the winner of the tender late on Wednesday or Thursday, said Vytenis Juevichius, director of the ministry's privatisation department.
But he added that the process may be delayed due to additional clarification from three or four of the candidates.
He also said that a runner up may be chosen in order to have a more competitive process.
"We are trying to have a better negotiating position with the winner to push him to reduce the price," he told Reuters.
"The commission decided that if we select one winner and enter into negotiations and they will not lower their price, then we will invite the second company," Junevichius said.
Financial and technical offers to act as the government's lead adviser in the privatisation were received from seven applicants by last week's deadline.

The applicants included Creditanstalt Invesment Bank, Union Bank of Switzerland, Banque Paribas and Cliford Chance, Flemings and Hansa Investments, Deutche Morgan Grenfell with Nomura International, N.M. Rothschild and Squire, Sanders and Dempsey and Daiwa.
Merrill Lynch was taken out of the running because its offer was received late.

The 100 percent state-run Lithuanian Telecom company is one of 13 key infrustructure enterprises slated for sale by Lithuania's right-of-centre government, which has vowed to speed the pace of privatisation.
The government said earlier it expected to start the actual privatisation of the firm early in 1998.
